concepts.why: The presence of bilateral adrenal and periaortic retroperitoneal masses, mild lymphocytopenia, and a sparse perivascular and interstitial infiltrate of enlarged atypical mononuclear cells suggests lymphoma.
The symptoms of intermittent fevers, episodic night sweats, and ill-defined erythema, edema, and tender induration are consistent with sarcoidosis.
The presence of elevated creatine kinase, aldolase, and lactate dehydrogenase, along with gastrocnemius myositis, suggests myositis.

The presence of bilateral adrenal and periaortic retroperitoneal masses, mild lymphocytopenia, and a sparse perivascular and interstitial infiltrate of enlarged atypical mononuclear cells suggests Castleman disease.

The presence of bilateral adrenal and periaortic retroperitoneal masses, mild lymphocytopenia, and a sparse perivascular and interstitial infiltrate of enlarged atypical mononuclear cells suggests histiocytosis.
The presence of moderate anemia suggests autoimmune hemolytic anemia.
The presence of elevated creatine kinase, aldolase, and lactate dehydrogenase, along with gastrocnemius myositis, suggests polymyositis.
The presence of ill-defined erythema, edema, and tender induration, along with elevated creatine kinase, aldolase, and lactate dehydrogenase, suggests dermatomyositis.

rationales.F01: Painful swelling and erythema suggest an inflammatory or malignant process, which could be seen in lymphoma or myositis.
rationales.F02: Bilateral adrenal and periaortic retroperitoneal masses are highly suggestive of lymphoma or Castleman disease.
rationales.F11: Elevated muscle enzymes indicate muscle damage, which is consistent with myositis or polymyositis.
rationales.F12: Atypical mononuclear cells in the skin biopsy are suggestive of a lymphoproliferative disorder, such as lymphoma.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of bilateral adrenal and periaortic retroperitoneal masses, intermittent fevers, episodic night sweats, and a sparse perivascular and interstitial infiltrate of enlarged atypical mononuclear cells in the reticular dermis and subcutis supports Lymphoma as the most likely diagnosis.
